transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-03 09:17 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Iyer (Redwood PM); Samir Patel (AtlasGrid Lead ML Eng), Ruth Kim (AtlasGrid Platform Eng), Jordan Lee (AtlasGrid Security), Emily Zhao (AtlasGrid Product)

Summary (auto): Demo of Redwood API + Console and Optimize focused on swapping AtlasGrid endpoints from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together into a unified Redwood endpoint. Covered parity mapping, token cost tradeoffs, routing, Dedicated trial, and security integrations. Agreed next steps and actions.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run through a swap playbook for unifying your endpoints into a single Redwood API. quick intros?
[00:12] Samir Patel: Samir here, lead on inference; we run a mix of OpenAI for chat, Anthropic for safety sensitive prompts, and a few Together endpoints for high-throughput batching. trying to consolidate costs and simplify routing.
[00:28] Maya Chen: great, and Ruth?
[00:31] Ruth Kim: Platform lead, i own infra & k8s glue. concerned about egress and our VPC peering, also key management.
[00:38] Jordan Lee: Jordan, security. SOC2 stuff, audit logs, SSO.
[00:42] Emily Zhao: product, curious about latency targets and user-visible regressions.
[00:47] Luis Ortega: thanks team. quick note we're gonna show the Redwood API call parity, then console rollout and Optimize recommendations for batching/quant. we'll flag places where behavior may vary and how to tune.

--- Demo: API parity mapping ---
[01:20] Luis Ortega: first, the request surface. OpenAI/Anthropic/Together all have similar fields but different names. we map them at the SDK layer: messages -> inputs, model alias, temperature, stop tokens. we'll show an example request mapping on-screen.
[01:42] (screen share starts)
[01:50] Luis Ortega: here's a sample Node snippet from your current OpenAI usage. notice role/system/user messages. in Redwood we preserve roles, but we also expose a streaming token hook and structured output enforcement to reduce hallucinations.
[02:10] Samir Patel: how does the delta look for our legacy streaming client? we use websocket style partials.
[02:15] Luis Ortega: Redwood supports chunked streaming over HTTP/2 and websocket emulation — you'd see identical chunk IDs in callbacks. a small adapter shim (we can share) converts your websocket partials to Redwood's stream. minimal code change.
[02:32] Ruth Kim: and stateful KV cache? our app pins a lot of context in KV cache between calls.
[02:40] Luis Ortega: yes, we have KV cache === KV cache (laugh), Redwood supports prefix caching and hot-cache routing. note: sometimes transcription shows 'key cash' but it's KV cache. you can persist cache to our optional persistent store on Dedicated.

[03:05] Maya Chen: on model variants, we support multi-variant routing. you might route Anthropic-equivalent models for safety-heavy routes and cheaper quantized variants for bulk embeddings. the console shows model families and compatibility notes.
[03:30] Emily Zhao: will output probabilities / logprobs match exactly between vendors?
[03:34] Luis Ortega: not guaranteed; tokenization differences and sampling can change logprobs. for most downstream metrics we see parity within tolerance. for exact reproducibility you can pin the request seeds and deterministic sampling, but that impacts creativity.

--- Console walkthrough: rollouts & routing ---
[07:12] (switching tabs)
[07:20] Priya Iyer: in console, here's a route config. you can define mapping rules: path /chat -> model family x, threshold latency 250ms, fallback to smaller model. also traffic split for canary 5%.
[07:45] Ruth Kim: what about region routing? we need EU data residency for some customers.
[07:50] Priya Iyer: we support region selectors; you can pin routes to eu-west or on-prem nodes. logs show which region served each call. for Private deployments, control plane can be customer-managed.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: audit logs detail? retention?
[08:09] Priya Iyer: audit logs include token-level metadata and are configurable retention 30/90/365 days as an add-on. we can redact prompt text in logs if needed and still retain tracing hooks.

[09:00] Maya Chen: about Dedicated trial we mentioned: we'll provision a small GPU pool in your CE region for two weeks to run parity and bench runs. this isolates your data.
[09:15] Samir Patel: will the Dedicated trial accept our SAML SSO and KMS?
[09:20] Maya Chen: yes, we can wire SAML for user access. for KMS, we support customer-managed keys (bring your own KMS) and HSM connectors — we'll need jwt/role bindings.

--- Technical deep dive: Optimize & batching ---
[12:55] Luis Ortega: Optimize will recommend batching sizes and quant profiles per-model based on your actual prompt histogram. i've pre-loaded a sample prompt distribution (we used anonymized examples from a similar fintech customer). it recommended per-route batch size 8 for heavy chat, and 64 for emb generation.
[13:20] Ruth Kim: but batching increases latency tail. our SLO is 200ms p95 for interactive chat.
[13:26] Luis Ortega: exactly — Optimize shows tradeoff curves. at batch=8 p95 jumps ~40ms but cost drops 18%. there's an autoscale policy to keep p95 under threshold with burst capacity.
[13:42] Samir Patel: and quantization? we've seen quality drops on some instr tuning tasks.
[13:47] Luis Ortega: Optimize suggests hybrid quant profiles: int8 for bulk completions, int4 for embeddings; for instruction-sensitive endpoints we lock to fp16 or q8 to avoid regressions. we also tie quality monitors to eval sets so regressions trigger alerts.

--- Security & compliance ---
[18:02] Jordan Lee: SOC2? audit certification?
[18:05] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. we can share the attestation and pen test summary.
[18:12] Jordan Lee: encryption in transit + at rest?
[18:15] Priya Iyer: TLS-1.2/1.3 in transit; at rest you can use customer KMS. for Private, you control key lifecycle. we also support field-level encryption for PII.
[18:30] Jordan Lee: any ATO complexities?
[18:33] Maya Chen: for gov-style ATOs we provide audit logs, artifact bundles, and help with evidence collection. timeline depends on your controls but we've supported multiple enterprise ATOs recently.

--- Integration concerns & edge cases ---
[22:00] Emily Zhao: what about prompt-formatting differences? e.g. Anthropic prefers assistant-message style vs OpenAI roles.
[22:06] Luis Ortega: we have an adapter layer in SDK that normalizes message formats. it can also inject system prompts and safety wrappers for Anthropics-equivalent flows. it won't be perfectly identical but we include unit tests in the repo to assert behavioral parity for your canonical prompts.
[22:28] Samir Patel: latency tests — how do we run head-to-head?
[22:33] Luis Ortega: we'll run a bench harness: same prompts, same VM region, dedicated GPU pool. we'll collect p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and failure/error rates. we recommend running during your traffic window as well.

--- Cost discussion ---
[29:15] Maya Chen: quick cost modeling. using your reported traffic, swapping embeddings to q4quant + caching reduced token-hours by ~34% for a reference customer. we'll share an itemized cost delta spreadsheet.
[29:34] Ruth Kim: curious on egress costs for cross-region failover.
[29:37] Priya Iyer: console shows estimated egress dollars per-fallback route; you can limit cross-region fallback or enable burst in-region first.

--- Live Q&A with small demos ---
[34:00] (Luis runs a live call)
[34:12] Luis Ortega: making a sample call to Redwood chat endpoint, streaming chunks now...
[34:25] (customers listen)
[34:45] Samir Patel: looks similar. latencies?
[34:49] Luis Ortega: that particular call was 88ms p50 from EU node, we have trace ids if you want to correlate.
[35:04] Jordan Lee: trace ids in logs — are they correlated to user ids?
[35:09] Priya Iyer: we recommend pseudonymized IDs in logs; we can correlate via internal mapping for debug under strict access controls.

--- Project constraints & timeline ---
[39:10] Emily Zhao: timeline — we need a pilot in prod within 8 weeks; stakeholders are product + infra + security.
[39:18] Maya Chen: realistic — pilot in 6–8 weeks if we run the Dedicated trial, collect benchmarks week 1–2, iterate on configs week 3–5, then a staged rollout.
[39:28] Samir Patel: resource ask: we'll need a runbook and small infra playbook for our SREs.
[39:33] Maya Chen: we'll provide a migration runbook, adapter snippets, and a sample CI test harness.

--- Closing recap ---
[47:40] Maya Chen: quick recap: we'll send parity checklist + sample adapter diff, provision Dedicated trial in CE, schedule bench, and share SOC2/KMS docs. agreed owners are in action items. anything else?
[47:58] Samir Patel: pls include example eval sets and example prompts for safety routes.
[48:05] Luis Ortega: noted — will include an example safety eval and regression scripts.
[48:12] Ruth Kim: please include network egress notes and VPC peering steps.
[48:16] Maya Chen: yep.
[48:20] Jordan Lee: i'll follow up with KMS vendor details.
[48:24] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench run.
[48:32] (meeting ends)

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (e.g., "key cash" for KV cache, "V-P-C" for VPC) and speaker attribution minor glitches. Natural speech pauses, clarifications, and overlapping talk present.
